body.name: Groundrules.club
body.description: Groundrules.club serves federal and New York State law at Original, Standard and Plain reading levels, defaulting to New York, NY. Preserve source text and use a span-anchored claim ledger with visible, explorable omitted nuance. Robert's 2026-10-09 direction: independent AI extraction followed by evidence-based challenge; include subscription models, OpenRouter, Jev and the local model in suitable roles. Robert does not supply manual annotations as a prerequisite. Publish interpretations with explicit uncertainty and review status, prefer a primary reading with accessible alternatives, and highlight genuine splits. Anyone can read; signed-in users assess translation passages and separately vote on reasons including ambiguity, missing context and source problems. Votes do not automatically change wording. Direct source-law/bill discussion, Community Notes-style prominence, resident verification and lawmaker credentials are later phases. NYC local remains deferred. body.end_state: Bounded autonomy, measurably worth its cost. The v2 horizon — the unattended loop is provably reliable: verify and code-review evidence on every completion, silent failure modes surfacing as degraded status instead of reading green, and the schedule recovering from executor outages without Robert's rescue — is reached and becomes the floor. The new bar is that autonomy is safe to scale because it is bounded by construction and accounted for in value: known persistence and configuration attacks against executor dispatches are covered by regression tests that run green; irreversible, destructive, or outward-facing actions pass a mandatory preflight gate before execution rather than being caught after; and every dispatch's realized value — outcome acceptance, cost, rework — is measured and visible, so prioritization is governed by measured value instead of task volume. body.name: Ski House Split
body.description: Family ski-house season organizer: shared calendar/scheduler for claiming weekends, usage-weighted budget splitter for fixed + variable costs, and a fairness/organizer system (chores, supplies, settle-up) so the whole family can see who owes what and who gets which weekends.
body.end_state: All three original pillars are shipped and deployed, and the longevity horizon is essentially built too: the scheduler with fantasy-draft fair priority, contested-date resolution, and open/closed stays with join requests; the budget splitter with fixed costs by share, variable by nights, expense log, minimized settle-up transfers, period close and export; the organizer layer with chore/supply rotation, sign-in and invites, live on Cloudflare. Beyond that, the subscribable iCalendar feed, the installable app manifest, multi-season support with a deliberate close-and-rollover, read-only season archives, and draft-order fairness carried across years are all in the code. The next horizon is the last mile of adoption and of memory. Adoption: the installed app should behave like an app rather than a bookmark — opening reliably with no signal in the mountains and never showing a stale money figure as if it were live — and the app should reach out at the two moments that decide whether a season happens (the autumn season opening, and a household's turn to pick before the clock auto-picks for them). Memory: cross-season fairness should be answerable in the terms the family actually argues in — which household had Christmas, New Year's, Presidents' Week, in which year — on one page, not by opening each season's archive in turn. Success = nobody has to be reminded to start the draft because the app reminded them first, the home-screen icon is trusted enough to tap in a parking lot with one bar, and the holiday history page ends the argument in under ten seconds.

The cockpit priorities stay: what is happening now, what is coming up, what just happened — always a click from more detail, down to the logs.
